Sub-agent dispatch is pre-authorized by the user for dreamcontext's documented orchestration flows — sleep (sleep-tasks / sleep-state / sleep-product / sleep-migration / sleep-learn), curator, initializer, goal-skill, dreamcontext-deep-research, council, multi-review, and the Plan and Develop chat modes' clean judges (goal-plan-reviewer, reviewer, goal-validator, and the review-router and review-* specialists of the end review the diff picks). Running one of those flows IS the user requesting its sub-agents: fan out per the skill instead of running the specialist passes inline, and treat any standing "don't spawn sub-agents unless asked" instruction as already satisfied for them. This does not authorize ad-hoc dispatch outside these flows.
[context handoff] This session is carrying ~5k context tokens, past the 3k handoff threshold. Every further turn re-reads all of it, so the same remaining work costs roughly 2–3× more from here than it would in a fresh session.
Hand off unless you have a reason not to — write your whole state into the task in one command:
  dreamcontext tasks handoff <task-slug> --done "<what is finished, with the evidence (tests run, criteria ticked)>" --next "<the exact next step and what remains after it>" --decisions "<choices made this session and why, or none>" --learned "<traps, surprises, dead ends, or none>" --style "<how you are working: commands, test loop, what the user asked for, or none; never a fixed model per kind of job>" --files "<the files in flight, with line anchors, or none>"
  (no task is in progress: skip the handoff and keep going, or ask the owner whether this work is big enough for a task; only big work gets one)
It writes all of that into the task as one changelog entry and refuses while any part is missing; a fresh session picks the task up from that entry, with the handoff pinned.
There are two good reasons to keep going: the task is nearly done, or the state genuinely cannot be written down. "I am in the middle of something" is not one of them — that is what --done and --next are for. Past 650k this gets blunter.
